ds: Criminals gain control of customer accounts through phishing, credential stuffing, SIM swap or malware, then change details and extract funds. Early detection relies on login, device and change-of-details signals.

src.t: UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (specify year, e.g. 2025)
FinCEN, Advisory to Financial Institutions on Cyber-Events and Cyber-Enabled Crime (FIN-2016-A005, 2016)
FFIEC, Authentication and Access to Financial Institution Services and Systems (2021)

cn.rt: Credential, SIM-swap and device takeover enabling payments, card use, fraudulent loan draws, redraw and term deposit break-outs.

rat: Credential/device compromise in digital and call-centre channels.

ind.n: Login from new device, country or emulator
ind.cx: Session originates from unfamiliar infrastructure, possibly using an emulator or anonymising proxy.
ind.ds: Session originates from a device, country, emulator or network not previously associated with the customer, including shortly after a phishing event.
ind.cn: Login from unfamiliar device, location or infrastructure

ind.n: Multiple failed logins followed by success
ind.cx: Credential stuffing or brute force pattern preceding successful access.
ind.ds: Repeated failed authentication attempts, often across accounts from one source, followed by successful access.

ind.n: Contact details or phone number changed then high-value payment
ind.cx: Email, phone or address updated minutes before outbound transactions.
ind.ds: Email, phone, address or statement delivery details are changed, especially shortly before unusual activity or redirecting mail to a third party.
ind.cn: Recent change of contact or delivery details

ind.n: SIM swap or number port detected
ind.cx: Telecom signals show recent SIM change before OTP-protected actions.
ind.ds: Mobile number is ported or SIM replaced shortly before one-time-passcode-protected actions or outbound transfers.
ind.cn: SIM swap or number port before transfers

ind.n: New payee added and funds drained rapidly
ind.cx: Attacker adds beneficiaries and transfers most of the balance in one session.
ind.ds: Attacker adds beneficiaries and transfers most of the balance in one session.

ind.n: Password reset or credential change from unrecognised channel
ind.cx: Self-service reset triggered from an unfamiliar environment.
ind.ds: Self-service reset triggered from an unfamiliar environment.

ind.n: Card replacement or wallet provisioning to new address
ind.cx: Attacker requests cards or tokens to alternate addresses.
ind.ds: Attacker requests cards or tokens to alternate addresses.
A new or low-activity account receives payments from several unrelated individuals who appear to be victims of fraud or phishing, followed by onward movement or cash-out.
ind.cn: Account receiving funds from multiple apparent fraud victims

ind.n: Session shows automated or scripted interaction
ind.cx: Non-human timing, headless browser or scripted API calls.
ind.ds: Non-human timing, headless browser or scripted API calls.

ctl.ds: Analyses typing, navigation, remote-access tooling, call-in-progress signals and deviation from baseline to spot coached, scripted or hijacked sessions. It detects coercion and takeover.

Fingerprints devices, IP addresses, emulators and network attributes to link applications, sessions and accounts and to flag shared or anomalous infrastructure. It exposes mule rings and multiple-account abuse.
Requires phishing-resistant authentication and additional verification on risky sessions, credential or payee changes and large payments. It blocks unauthorised access and payments.
Rules that alert on abnormal count, value or speed of movements over defined windows compared with customer profile and peer norms. They provide baseline coverage across many typologies.

ctl.n: Account detail change monitoring and cool-down
ctl.ds: Contact, device or payee changes trigger notification to the prior channel and restrict risky actions for a short period, with alerts on clusters of changes. It disrupts takeover.

ctl.n: Cooling-off and delayed release for new payees
ctl.ds: Holds or delays the first large payment to a new payee or to changed details so the customer or institution can verify before funds leave. It buys time to detect coercion or fraud.

Matches accounts, devices, identifiers and beneficiaries against industry fraud sharing and ingests law-enforcement, commercial and open-source threat feeds, including victim reports from other institutions. It catches known bad actors early.

ctl.n: Funds hold, freeze and recall procedure
ctl.ds: Provides a defined, legally grounded capability to restrict, hold, freeze or recall funds and accounts pending review or on confirmed exposure, with clear triggers and approvers. It stops onward dissipation of suspected illicit funds.
Model that scores inbound-then-outbound pass-through, new-payee churn, counterparty diversity and profile mismatch to flag likely mule accounts. It prioritises accounts for review and restriction.
